title: 2026 In Vivo Magnetic Resonance Gordon Research Conference and Gordon Research Seminar
text:
We are requesting support for trainees to attend a scientific Gordon Research conference (GRC) focused on
advancing Magnetic Resonance (MR) imaging, a key technology used to diagnose and study many health
conditions. The conference is designed to foster focused discussion of cutting-edge research advances in the
MR field and provide mentorship for trainees so they can help shape the future of MR. By bringing together
experts and early-career researchers to share new ideas and innovations such as faster imaging, better
hardware, and AI tools, this GRC will help improve MR’s effectiveness in clinical care and public health.

title: Microbiome Discovery and Mechanisms to Combat Antibiotic Resistance at Mucosal Surfaces
text:
Project narrative.
Antibiotics are wonder drugs that have tamed bacterial infections over the past century.
Unfortunately, pathogens are now becoming resistant to the best antibiotics used in
clinical practice today. This project is aimed at identifying non-antibiotic strategies to
prevent and treat bacterial infections. Successful execution of this project will add to the
arsenal of tools we have to fight bacterial infections.

title: Molecular and Functional Mechanisms Underlying Cortical Activity in CACNA1A Epilepsy
text:
CACNA1A mutations are an underdiagnosed cause of severe, treatment-resistant, early-onset
epilepsy and other neurological disorders including familial hemiplegic migraine type 1, episodic
ataxia type 2, and spinocerebellar ataxia type 6. This proposal will use the first human-derived, three-
dimensional model system of CACNA1A to investigate effects of loss-of-function and gain-of-function
mutations on functional activity and gene expression in excitatory and inhibitory cortical neurons.
These experiments may reveal how excitation/inhibition imbalance—a common feature among
genetic epilepsies and other neurodevelopmental disorders—emerges in developing cortical circuitry,
paving a path for identifying novel therapeutic targets and variant classification criteria immediately
relevant to the CACNA1A community.

title: Dynamic FOXP3 Expression in the Development of Regulatory T cells from Induced Pluripotent Stem Cells
text:
Regulatory T cells (Tregs) suppress immune activation and inflammation and represent an attractive substrate
for adoptive cell therapy in autoimmune diseases. Current bottlenecks exist in utilizing Tregs as therapy due to
their rarity and unstable suppressive function. This proposal will study the role of endogenous and exogenous
expression of FOXP3 – the master transcription factor of Tregs – in the development of thymic-like Tregs from
an inexhaustible source: induced pluripotent stem cells.

title: High-Dimensional Immune Monitoring of NCI-Supported Immunotherapy Trials
text:
Through rigorous implementation of state-of-the-art, cross-compared technological platforms, we aim to
accelerate identification of clinically actionable biomarkers of response, resistance, and adverse events, and
define mechanisms at play to guide and improve novel NCI-supported cancer immunotherapy clinical trials.

title: Consortium of Food Allergy Research Clinical Research Center at Cincinnati Children's Hospital Medical Center (CoFAR-CRC:CCHMC)
text:
The proposed Consortium of Food Allergy Research Clinical Research Center: Cincinnati Children's Hospital
Medical Center (CoFAR-CRC:CCHMC) aims to bring the experience, expertise, and scientific productivity and
the diverse patient populations of CCHMC to CoFAR. The CoFAR-CRC:CCHMC approach to research is
multipronged and self-sustaining by attracting patients with excellent care and creating and maintaining
databases and registries supported by biospecimen collection and biobanking. Those are utilized in conducting
mechanistic research that forms the basis of discoveries and clinical trials and advances knowledge that
improves patient care and attracts more patients.

title: Single Molecule Detection of L1 Insertions and Intermediates
text:
This project will develop new tools to assess contributions of the LINE-1 (L1) retrotransposon to somatic
mosaicism in normal human tissues. Advances here will allow investigators to characterize L1 insertions
genome-wide using state-of-the-art long-read and single cell technologies. If successful, the project will enable
the Somatic Mosaicism across Human Tissues (SMaHT) Network to develop more complete catalogs of
genetic variation in tissues.

title: NeuroSync: a data-driven, music-based augmented reality neurorehabilitation platform of games & puzzles to stimulate neuroplasticity and prolong functional independence in Alzheimer's Disease patients
text:
Recent insights into the pathogenesis of Alzheimer’s Disease (AD) suggest therapies that enhance
neuroplasticity will play a key role in future treatment approaches that slow and/or reverse its progression
.
Towards this end, Outlier Technology, LLC is developing NeuroSync: a novel, Neurologic Music Therapy (NMT)-
based neurorehabilitation platform that offers
a structured program of adaptive, personalized evidence-based
interventions that evoke a unique combination of nostalgia, active music creation, movement, pattern recognition,
and cognitive challenges to stimulate neuroplasticity and stabilize and/or improve metrics of neurological health
and quality of life. This technology will 1) make personalized music-based neurological care more accessible to
AD patient-caregiver dyads and 2) offer analytics and decision support tools to providers; to bridge the gap
between therapies traditionally administered in clinical settings with those that can be safely used at-home,
offering a groundbreaking and affordable new approach that empowers users to “play” their way to better health.

title: Characterizing genetic signatures of natural selection to understand human diseases
text:
Characterizing genetic signatures of natural selection on the human genome is fundamental to understand
human evolutionary history and human diseases. In this proposal, we will develop and apply methods aiming at
characterize the genetic signatures of natural selection (1) shaping the genetic architecture of human complex
traits, (2) leading to different gene regulation and allele effect sizes across diverse ancestry groups, and (3)
acting on genes at the exon and regulatory levels. To reach that goal, we will leverage large GWAS datasets, a
new powerful conservation dataset, and multi-ancestry single-cell sequencing dataset.

title: Antiviral Countermeasures Development Center (AC/DC)
text:
The COVID-19 pandemic has called to global attention the unmitigated threat posed by emerging and re-
emerging zoonotic RNA viruses to human health, societies, and the global economy. The development of next
generation orally bioavailable direct-acting antivirals to prevent or mitigate disease, interrupt community
transmission chains, and potentially silence a nascent pandemic is imperative. Building on extensive expertise
in antiviral drug development and a panel of initial lead chemotypes, the Antiviral Countermeasures
Development Center will identify and develop orally efficacious direct-acting nucleoside analog and non-
nucleoside small-molecule antivirals to clinical candidate stage.

title: Animal Core
text: Project Summary – Animal Core (C001) The inclusion of an Animal Core (C001) in this Center renewal reflects the needs of a research enterprise with a focus on shared genetic mouse models and demands for standardized and integrated behavioral phenotyping. To address these requirements, C001 will 1) establish, maintain and distribute genetic mouse models; 2) conduct standard operating procedures (SOPs) for behavioral and cognitive phenotypes under study by PARC Research Projects; and 3) utilize the already established pipeline for sequencing sample database integration and sample submission for sequencing to the Integrated Genomics Laboratory. Centralizing these activities within C001 will strengthen research outcomes by ensuring that uniform methods are applied to mouse production and phenotyping, and to sample acquisition and preservation. Furthermore, data will be preserved in an already established electronic database that can be easily shared. This uniformity in resources and services is vital for the integration of data by the Bioinformatics Core C002 across research projects and will enhance Centeredness and the potential for synergistic outcomes. In addition, the Animal Core will reduce research costs through an economy of scale. C001 will collaborate with the Research Projects in the completion of four Specific Aims. In Aim 1, the Core will establish, maintain and distribute the Diversity Outbred (DO) mice, and the selectively bred High EtOH Preference (HP) mouse line. In Aim 2, the Core will perform behavioral phenotyping services, including a standardized 2-bottle choice (2BC) procedure for the measurement of chronic EtOH intake and follow-up measures as needed when manipulations are found to alter EtOH intake or cognitive measures. In Aim 3, a digging Attentional Set-Shifting Task that was established by the PARC within C001, will be used to measure cognitive flexibility in the DO and HP mice and to measure the effects of chronic EtOH drinking. This task was designed to closely parallel cognitive flexibility testing performed in rhesus macaques in which poor cognitive flexibility was found to predict high EtOH drinking and to be a result of high EtOH drinking. Testing of the HP line and of individual DO mice that will vary in EtOH intake will provide cross-species translation of these findings. In addition, C001 will work with P004 to determine relationships among chronic EtOH drinking, cognitive flexibility, and the hyaluronan-based extracellular matrix. Data will also be used by P002 to examine potential relationships with glutamate and GABA dynamics. Finally, in Aim 4, for P001, the Animal Core will utilize an already established pipeline for sequencing sample integration into PARC databases and for submission of snRNA-Seq samples for next- generation sequencing services. Data from the OHSU Integrated Genomics Laboratory centralized service will be transmitted to the Bioinformatics Core (C002) for alignment and initial analysis and C002 will work with P001 for subsequent analyses and interpretation.

title: Bioinformatics, Data Analytics and Predictive Modeling
text: The Bioinformatics, Data Analytics and Predictive Modeling Core has two primary objectives: i) to assist the Center users with bioinformatics, statistical, and programming needs, and ii) to develop and facilitate access to insightful analytical and predictive resources that enable the mining of high-throughput transcriptomic, proteomic, and metabolomic experiments. Working closely with the Sampling and Separation and Molecular Profiling and Characterization Cores, our data analyses enhance the understanding of cell-cell signaling mechanisms associated with drug abuse and pain perception. The Bioinformatics Core stands out as a global leader in annotating neuropeptide genes and their corresponding peptide products, and developing web services that support research on neuropeptide, proteoform, and protein complex identification, quantification, and annotation. Core products include the development and continuous update of comprehensive catalogs of neuropeptide genes and products, proteoforms, and metabolites. The Bioinformatics Core’s impact is profound, as evidenced by the number of publication citations and active utilization of the core's web services, including NeuroPred, neuroProSight, PepShop, TDPortal, and the Human and Mouse Brain Proteoform Atlases, demonstrating the ongoing demand for our bioinformatic and analytical services. Moving forward, the primary mission of this core remains the support of Center users in the design and analysis of data from high-throughput ‘omic experiments planned to test hypotheses about molecular processes associated with cell-cell signaling, drug abuse, and pain perception. To address existing gaps in high-throughput ‘omic research of the molecular processes underlying cell-cell signaling, drug abuse, and pain perception, the Bioinformatics Core has outlined the following specific aims: 1) advance the understanding of targeted molecules and biomarkers through multi-omics analysis at both single-cell and aggregate level supported by user-friendly web services; 2) assist preclinical breakthroughs by providing enriched annotation of key molecules, their isoforms, and networks; 3) precisely characterize proteoforms and protein complexes; and 4) prepare and empower junior researchers to employ bioinformatics resources through educational materials and training. The proposed activities address the surge in demand for artificial intelligence-guided analysis of ‘omic data driven by advancements that yield vast amounts of information, such as the transition from bulk to single-cell and spatial transcriptomics, epigenomics, proteomics, and metabolomics. Our core excels in developing bioinformatics pipelines that integrate information across platforms and employs Big Data to Knowledge approaches to capture multi-omic data signals and variability, and sift through noise. The Bioinformatics Core’s innovation hinges on facilitating the exploration of transcript, peptide, and metabolic isoforms that significantly impact drug abuse and pain perception. While the primary focus is on unraveling the molecular mechanisms of drug abuse and pain, the core’s efforts are expected to advance research in other physiological and behavioral disorders.

title: Mechanistic studies of nucleic acid enzymes involved in DNA replication, transcription, and innate immunity
text:
This research will enhance fundamental understanding of how helicases and polymerases regulate innate
immune responses and mitochondrial gene expression and replication. Insights into RNA sensing by RIG-I-like
receptors may lead to new strategies for optimizing immune responses in inflammatory diseases and
immunotherapy. Understanding the mechanisms of mitochondrial transcription and DNA replication may guide
therapeutic approaches for mitochondrial disorders and cancers with altered mitochondrial function.

title: Dissecting the Cellular and Molecular Mechanisms Underpinning Single Neuron Computation
text:
PIs:Clandinin and Druckmann
 The transformation of synaptic inputs into axonal outputs within single neurons represents a
fundamental building block of brain computation. This project dissects and models the cellular and
molecular mechanisms that control how single neurons compute. These studies will reveal generalizable
principles underpinning single neuron computation and will build robust biophysical models that can be used
to explore circuit function in both health and neurological disease.

title: Addressing the research-practice gap in the implementation of rapid whole genome sequencing in the NICU
text:
While studies confirm that rapid whole genome sequencing accelerates diagnoses and life-saving therapies in
critically ill newborns, its adoption in clinical setting is lagging. We propose a dissemination and implementation
science project to improve adoption of genome sequencing in Level 4 (tertiary, metropolitan, higher resourced)
and Level 3 (non-tertiary, rural, lower resourced) neonatal intensive care units.

title: Mentoring in clinical trials and patient-oriented research in infectious diseases and global health
text:
The goal of this proposal is to mentor young investigators with the skills and experience required to become a
successful independent investigator in patient-oriented research in global health and infectious diseases, and
to provide the support and tools to sustain their passion on this pathway and beyond. Mentoring of trainees will
occur in the context of the candidate’s successful clinical trial program, which includes individual and cluster
randomized controlled trials to evaluate the impact of novel interventions to reduce and eliminate malaria
disease burden and transmission. New research is proposed in surveillance of malaria and other pathogens
using genomics and serology to inform clinical care and public health strategies to manage malaria and febrile
illness in children.

title: Project-003
text: (Overall) This is a program project grant that is centered on improving our understanding of how immune dysregulation can arise and lead to autoimmunity and inflammation. The results of the projects here will help improve our ability to both detect and devise logical treatment strategies for autoimmunity and immune dysregulation.

title: Deep T-Cell Receptor profiling using droplet PCR and Sloppy Molecular Beacons
text:
The normally immense diversity of the T-cell receptor (TCR) repertoire, which is crucial for proper immune
function, diminishes in many disease states, including in T-cell lymphomas, due to the expansion of certain
T-cell clones. Currently, next-generation sequencing is the mainstay of diagnostics, but its clinical adoption is
limited by high costs, complexity, and technical challenges. To address this need, this project aims to develop
a rapid, low-cost method that utilizes innovative sloppy molecular beacon probes, single-cell droplet PCR,
and melt profile analysis through machine learning to assess the TCR repertoire at high depth.

title: Systems genomics of complex traits
text:
Despite notable successes of identifying the genetic basis in some human diseases, most diseases are
generated by complex interactions between multiple genes and the environment. New approaches using
comprehensive whole-genome sequencing and genomic engineering methods in model organisms provide the
opportunity to make rapid progress in understanding the underlying bases of this complexity. Using natural
populations of species with extreme genetic variation provides an opportunity to identify unique regulatory
elements and systems whose functional impacts would otherwise be hidden to us.
